metric.why: Distributed AI training is unusually intolerant of network degradation; a lossy fabric shows up as wasted GPU-hours before it shows up as an outage.
metric.metric: Network latency, packet loss, and bandwidth
metric.definition: Continuous measurement of round-trip latency, loss rate, and utilization on the facility's internal fabric and external transit.

reading.body:
Network latency, packet loss, and bandwidth degradation waste GPU compute hours before triggering outages, making continuous fabric monitoring essential for AI training facilities.

Distributed AI training distributes work across many GPUs, which means the network becomes a critical path. A single point of congestion or packet loss does not stop the system immediately. Instead, it forces GPUs to wait for data, turning expensive compute into idle time. This efficiency loss accumulates across thousands of processors before any alert fires. Operators measure round-trip latency, loss rates, and utilization on both internal fabric and external transit to catch this degradation early, when it still shows in metrics but before it breaks the training run.

This matters specifically because AI workloads are unusually intolerant of network problems compared to traditional datacenter tasks. Batch processing and storage systems can absorb latency and retransmit without cascading failures. GPU clusters cannot. The data here measures what matters: continuous observation of the paths data takes between machines, not just whether the network is up.

The data does not cover network architecture itself, fiber paths, or the specific technologies used to carry traffic. It tracks symptoms, not infrastructure.
